mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5%, it signals a tight labor market that supports strong corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances when UNRATE < 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals that the Fed is responding to inflation, which may lead to a temporary market correction (negative returns) over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not significant (p-value > 0.05) in a regression of 20-day returns on the interaction term over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO), the S&P 500 tends to underperform (negative returns) over the next 60 days, as it signals an economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1600 thousand units signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances when HOUST < 1600.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days because it supports consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS growth and 5-day SPX returns is not significant (p-value > 0.05) over the last 3 years.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong retail sales (RSAFS) and a high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals that the economy is strong but the Fed is restrictive, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: strong economy with restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: The interaction term (RSAFS * FEDFUNDS) has a positive coefficient in a regression of 20-day returns, or the effect is not significant (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative returns over the next 60 days as the Fed raises rates to combat inflation.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY.
